<NewDataSet>
  <IIRIncidentBrief>
    <OwningUnitId>3933532</OwningUnitId>
    <StartDtTm>2023-04-15T23:32:00-04:00</StartDtTm>
    <IncidentBrief>On April 15, 2023, at approximately 1635 PST, the Washington State Ferry WALLA WALLA (O.N. 546382) was underway from Bremerton to Seattle when the engineering crew responded to a low frequency alarm on the #1 ship service diesel generator (SSDG). The #1 SSDG and Vital Generator were operating in parallel. The crew identified the problem as low fuel pressure on the #1SSDG. The crew started the #2 SSDG in an attempt to transfer the electrical load of the vessel from the #1 SSDG to the #2 SSDG. While waiting for the #2 SSDG to come up to temperature, the #1 SSDG fuel pressure was manually increased with the hand priming pump. Without an installed fuel pressure gauge the crew couldn’t determine the accurate fuel pressure on the engine and stopped priming the engine. Shortly after stopping priming, the #1 SSDG tripped offline due to low fuel pressure. The electrical protective measure in place, the Vital bus tie disconnect breaker, did not operate as designed and caused the Vital generator to trip offline. This caused the vessel to lose all power, propulsion and steering. 

The vessel’s emergency generator came online as designed and the vessel was able to regain steering. Without propulsion the Master had to decide whether to ground the vessel at a known and approved intentional grounding spot or turn to STBD into Rich Passage with no propulsion. The vessel deployed the port anchor in an attempt to slow the vessel. The vessel grounded at Pleasant Beach on Bainbridge Island with a full carload and approximately 698 passengers. The vessel implemented its casualty control procedures and passengers’ assembled at station #1 and donned life vests. At approximately 1900, the evacuation of all passengers was started with Kitsap Transit vessels.
 
The engineering crew was unable to get propulsion restored before the tide went out to far. The vessel had to wait for the tide to come back up and get towed off the beach. The vessel was able to get propulsion restored and moored safely back in Bremerton.

As a result of this casualty, fuel pressure gauges were reinstalled in the engine control room, changes have been implemented to lower the number of hours between fuel filter changes, and the process has been updated on using the fuel oil purifiers. Additionally, all engineers on all sister vessels were briefed on incident and on the corrective actions were being implemented.

As a result of this investigation, the Coast Guard determined that the initiating event for this casualty was the clogging of the fuel filters on the #1 SSDG which lead to the loss of vessel propulsion. The casual factors that contributed to this casualty include: (1) the lack of installed fuel pressure gauges, (2) the operator’s failure to monitor the generators’ fuel pressures, (3) the vital bus tie disconnect breaker not operating properly, (4) the lack of readiness of the standby generator to not be up to temperature to take the load, and (5) the lack of adequate casualty control procedures.</IncidentBrief>
  </IIRIncidentBrief>
</NewDataSet>

<NewDataSet>
  <IIRIncidentBrief>
    <OwningUnitId>3933532</OwningUnitId>
    <StartDtTm>2022-08-13T20:35:00-04:00</StartDtTm>
    <IncidentBrief>On August 13, 2022, at approximately 1335 local time, the tribal fishing vessel ALEUTIAN ISLE (O.N. 558156) sank in 120 feet of water while fishing off the North end of San Juan Island in Puget Sound.

The ALEUTIAN ISLE is a 58-foot 62 gross ton multi-purpose fishing vessel registered to the Swinomish Tribe and documented by the Coast Guard with Fishery, Registry, and Coastwise endorsements.  The crew at the time of the incident consisted of a Captain, three crewmembers, and one passenger. Neither the Captain nor crew held Coast Guard Merchant Mariner Credentials. 

On August 12, 2022, at approximately 1400 local time, while getting underway to test their new fishing gear, the ALEUTIAN ISLE ran aground at the entrance of the Cap Sante Marina. The vessel was able to free itself from the grounding. Once in safe water, they deployed the net and conducted a complete inspection of the vessel. There was no damage or pollution as a result of the grounding earlier in the day. The vessel continued the testing of its fishing gear and at approximately 2400 local time, the vessel anchored in Griffin Bay for the night.

On August 13, 2022, at approximately 0400 local time the crew of the ALEUTIAN ISLE started the main propulsion engine and began preparing the vessel to get underway. At approximately 0420 they pulled the anchor and were underway bound for the south end of San Juan Island to fish for salmon. They arrived at the fishing grounds around 0700 and set their nets. The vessel completed four set/hauls before they decided to relocate. At approximately 1000 the vessel got underway bound for the new fishing grounds on the north end of the San Juan Island.

At around 1100, while in transit to the new fishing grounds, the engine room high bilge level alarm activated, audibly and visually alerting the crew to a problem in the engine room.

The captain went to the engine room to investigate the bilge level alarm and found a few inches of water in the bilge and pumped it overboard using the bilge pump. He also discovered the fish hold chiller pump motor circuit breaker in the tripped position and reset it. At approximately 1200 the vessel arrived at the new fishing grounds and waited for the tide to change to begin fishing.

At approximately 1320 one of the crewmembers notified the captain that the vessel was riding low by the stern. The captain investigated and found water washing over the stern. At that time, he did not notice any water intrusion in the engine room. With the vessel becoming unstable, the captain attempted to restore vessel freeboard by pumping the fish hold. In preparation for a possible abandon ship, one of the crewmembers boarded the sein skiff and cut it away from the ALEUTIAN ISLE.

At approximately 1330 the ALEUTIAN ISLE started listing to port. As the angle increased the cargo and net shifted to further to port and increased the listing angle. As the listing angle increased, down flooding began with water entering the ALEUTIAN ISLE through the port side ventilation intakes and main deck door leading to the galley. Once the water entered the galley it had free communication to the engine room and main cabin berthing areas. The down flooding caused ALEUTIAN ISLE to roll hard over on its port side. The remaining crewmembers and passenger made their way to the starboard side of the vessel, which was still out of the water and were rescued by the skiff.

At approximately 1335 local time the ALEUTIAN ISLE sank in 120 feet of water and was declared a complete loss.

As a result of its investigation, the Coast Guard determined that the initiating event for this marine casualty to be failure of the PVC piping in the lazarette space for the fish hold fill and chiller water. The causal factors contributing to this casualty include: (1) Debris in the Lazarette clogging bilge drainage. (2) No high-level bilge alarm in the lazarette. (3) The loss of stability due to the flooding of the lazarette.</IncidentBrief>
  </IIRIncidentBrief>
</NewDataSet>

responses.brief:
<NewDataSet>
  <IIRIncidentBrief>
    <OwningUnitId>3933532</OwningUnitId>
    <StartDtTm>2023-04-08T10:00:00-04:00</StartDtTm>
    <IncidentBrief>On April 7, 2023, the KODIAK ENTERPRISE (O.N. 579450), a United States flagged commercial fishing-processing vessel, was moored at the Trident Seafoods Corporation facility in Tacoma, Washington on the Hylebos Waterway. The vessel had been pier side since March 24, 2023, undergoing a scheduled dockside maintenance period consisting of multiple hot work projects (grinding, cutting, welding), and other various tasks onboard.  

Following the workday, three crewmembers remained onboard the KODIAK ENTERPRISE for the night. At approximately 0300 local time (LT) on April 8, 2023, a crew crewmember aboard another vessel that was moored at the same facility observed smoke coming from the KODIAK ENTERPRISE and reported it to the facility security guard. The security guard called 911 and Tacoma Fire Department responded to the scene. The security guard also called one of the crewmembers onboard the KODIAK ENTERPRISE, waking him up and alerting him of the fire onboard.  

The three crewmembers safely escaped without injury and remained on scene to assist and direct the initial firefighting response. Despite intensive efforts, fire fighters were unable to control the fire. Approximately 12 hours after firefighting began, active firefighting efforts concluded and defensive firefighting tactics employed, focusing on cooling the vessel from the outside to minimize fire spread and any impact to the environment outside of the vessel. The fire continued to burn for approximately seven days when on scene responders declared the fire extinguished on April 14, 2023, at approximately 1600 LT. The vessel was a total constructive loss estimated at approximately $150 million.   

As a result of its investigation, the Coast Guard determined that the initiating event of the casualty was the ignition of combustible materials within the dry stores area of the vessel. This led to the subsequent spread of the fire resulting in the total constructive loss of the vessel. Due to the seven-day burn period and extensive damage to the vessel, investigators were unable to definitely determine the causal factor(s) that contributed to the casualty. The two most probable causal factors of the fire were: (1) Failure of the shipyard personnel conducting hot work to take actions to prevent sparks or hot debris from entering the dry stores loading hatch, and (2) Failure of electrical equipment within the dry stores area that caused ignition of surrounding combustible materials. The primary causal factor of the subsequent constructive loss was: (1) Failure of the vessel’s fire alarm system to wake sleeping crewmembers and provide immediate notification of a fire onboard the vessel.</IncidentBrief>
  </IIRIncidentBrief>
</NewDataSet>

responses.brief:
<NewDataSet>
  <IIRIncidentBrief>
    <OwningUnitId>3933532</OwningUnitId>
    <StartDtTm>2024-07-23T19:11:00-04:00</StartDtTm>
    <IncidentBrief>On 23 July 2024 at approximately 1111 local time, the cruise ship EURODAM (9378448) lost propulsion in Glacier Bay National Park, Alaska. EURODAM had two generators (DG1 & DG4) of the vessel's six main diesel generators connected to the vessel's 11 kv switchboard which controlled the port and starboard azipod propulsion motors, when it experienced the loss of propulsion. The engineers onboard the vessel experienced an alarm in the engine control room that one of the two running main diesel generators (DG4) had disconnected from the switchboard. DG1 continued to run and stayed connected to the switchboard providing electrical power to the ship. However, due to the inadequate load distribution, the ship's preferential trip system activated and high electrical consumers were shutdown to include the azipod motors. The vessel continued its forward momentum but had no maneuverability. The vessel retained electrical power (minus the azipod motors, A/C compressors, and galley services) and the engineering crew began to troubleshoot. The engineers observed the forward and aft high voltage switchboard breakers tripped during power fluctuations and they manually closed them to restore power to the high voltage switchboards. They started a standby diesel generator and regained power and propulsion. When they regained propulsion, the vessel "station kept" in order to verify no further electrical disruptions prior to continuing the transit. The vessel proceeded on its intended voyage and completed repairs in Seattle, Washington on 07 September 2024.

Through its investigation, the Coast Guard has determined the initiating event for this casualty to be a faulty control card on DG1's governor which caused DG4 to disconnect from the switchboard and trip the azipod electrical motors which resulted in a loss of propulsion. Causal factors contributing to this casualty include: 1) a faulty load control card on DG1's governor.

EURODAM representatives failed to reasonably notify the nearest Coast Guard (Sector Southeast Alaska) Officer in Charge, Marine Inspection of the casualty as required per 46CFR4.05-1(a). The casualty occurred on 23 July 2024 at approximately 1111 local time and the vessel's crew notified District 17's public affairs office via their shared mailbox on 25 July 2024 at 1050 local time.</IncidentBrief>
  </IIRIncidentBrief>
</NewDataSet>

  <IIRIncidentBrief>
    <OwningUnitId>3933532</OwningUnitId>
    <StartDtTm>2017-08-23T16:30:00-04:00</StartDtTm>
    <IncidentBrief>On August 23, 2017, at approximately 0830, MSD Sitka received a report of a discharge of hydraulic oil in the the water creating a sheen on Sitka Sound which is a U.S. navigable waterway. The Responsible Party (RP) has been identified as the Holland America Lines, the owner of the EURODAM, and a Notice of Federal Interest has been issued. The discharged occurred while conducting routine maintenance on the port side drop down tender ramp. A hose fitting on the forward hydraulic ram arm was identified as the source of the discharge and has been repaired. It was estimated that 1 Liter of oil discharged into the water.</IncidentBrief>
  </IIRIncidentBrief>
</NewDataSet>

<NewDataSet>
  <IIRIncidentBrief>
    <OwningUnitId>3933532</OwningUnitId>
    <StartDtTm>2018-07-14T21:45:00-04:00</StartDtTm>
    <IncidentBrief>On July 14, 2018 at approximately 1445 local time a elderly female passenger (US Citizen) was injured aboard the EURODAM (ON:9378448) she was walking down the stairs from Deck 3 to Deck 2 Amidships stairwell when she missed the last step resulting in injury.  The vessel was moored in Seattle, WA at the time of the incident.  The passenger was transported to Ballard Swedish Hospital where she was diagnosed with a broken ankle, she received a cast on her left ankle and then was released.

As a result of its investigation the Coast Guard has determined that the initiating event for this casualty was, passenger falling on the landing between the 2nd and 3rd deck, injuring her ankle. The causal factor that contributed to this casualty was, passenger had difficulty seeing stair step due the use of multi distance glasses.</IncidentBrief>
  </IIRIncidentBrief>
</NewDataSet>
